linear-function.name: Linear function
linear-function.oneLiner: The most basic function, whose graph is a straight line proportional to x
linear-function.description: The linear function y = ax + b changes y by the same amount a every time x increases by 1. Its graph is always a straight line, where a is the slope and b is the y-intercept.
linear-function.significance: It is where the study of functions begins, and the most basic tool for expressing any phenomenon whose rate of change stays constant.

a.description: It says how steep the line is. Positive tilts it up to the right, negative down to the right.

b.description: The y-coordinate of the point where the line meets the y-axis. It is also the value of y when x is 0.

x.description: The input value, which you are free to choose.

y.description: The output value, decided by the value of x.

realWorldExamples: A taxi fare made up of a base fare plus a charge per distance
The time-distance relation for someone walking at a steady speed

slope-formula.name: Slope formula
slope-formula.oneLiner: The formula for the slope of a line from the coordinates of two points
slope-formula.description: The slope formula m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1) works out how steep the line through two points on the coordinate plane is. It gives the change in y against the change in x — that is, the rate of change.
slope-formula.significance: It puts the direction and steepness of a line into a precise number, and leads naturally into the rate of change that underlies differentiation.

m.description: The value that says how steep the line is.

x_1.description: The horizontal position of the first point.

y_1.description: The vertical position of the first point.

x_2.description: The horizontal position of the second point.

y_2.description: The vertical position of the second point.

realWorldExamples: Working out the gradient of a mountain path
The rate of rise over a given period on a stock chart

point-slope-form.name: Point-slope form
point-slope-form.oneLiner: The form that gives the equation of a line when you know one point and the slope
point-slope-form.description: The point-slope form y - y1 = m(x - x1) lets you write down the equation of a line straight away once you know one point (x1, y1) on it and the slope m.
point-slope-form.significance: It is the most practical form for finding the equation of a line, and it is the form used for the equation of a tangent line in calculus.

x_1.description: The horizontal position of a point confirmed to lie on the line.

y_1.description: The vertical position of a point confirmed to lie on the line.

realWorldExamples: A model predicting future temperature from the current temperature and its rate of change
An expression for a sales trend built from sales at one moment and the growth rate

quadratic-standard.name: Standard form of a quadratic function
quadratic-standard.oneLiner: The basic form of the quadratic function, whose graph is a parabola
quadratic-standard.description: The standard form of a quadratic function, y = ax² + bx + c, contains x squared, and its graph is a parabola. The sign of a decides whether the curve opens downward or upward.
quadratic-standard.significance: It is the key function for describing many everyday phenomena, from projectile motion to maximum and minimum problems.

a.description: It decides the direction and width of the parabola. Positive opens upward, negative opens downward.

b.description: It affects where the axis of the parabola sits.

c.description: The y-coordinate of the point where the parabola meets the y-axis.

realWorldExamples: How the height of a thrown ball changes
The curve of an arch in a bridge

quadratic-vertex.name: Vertex form of a quadratic function
quadratic-vertex.oneLiner: The form of a quadratic function in which the coordinates of the vertex are visible at once
quadratic-vertex.description: The vertex form of a quadratic function, y = a(x - h)² + k, shows at a glance that the vertex of the parabola is (h, k). You reach this form by completing the square on the standard form.
quadratic-vertex.significance: Because it hands you the maximum or minimum of the function directly, it is central to solving optimisation problems.

a.description: It decides the direction and width of the parabola. It is the same a as in the standard form.

h.description: Where the axis of symmetry of the parabola sits.

k.description: The minimum (when a > 0) or maximum (when a < 0) of the parabola.

realWorldExamples: Finding the highest point a fountain's jet of water reaches
Finding the price that maximises profit when setting the price of a product

discriminant.name: Discriminant
discriminant.oneLiner: The expression that tells you in advance how many roots a quadratic equation has
discriminant.description: The discriminant D = b² - 4ac lets you judge the number and kind of roots of the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 without solving it. If D is positive there are two distinct roots, if it is 0 there is a repeated root, and if it is negative there are no real roots.
discriminant.significance: By letting you judge whether solutions exist before you solve the equation, it plays a key part in deciding how to approach a problem.

D.description: The sign of this value decides the number and kind of the roots.

b.description: The number multiplying x in the quadratic equation.

a.description: The number multiplying x squared in the quadratic equation.

c.description: The number added in the quadratic equation with no variable attached.

realWorldExamples: Judging whether a thrown ball can reach a certain height
Checking whether two curves have a point of intersection

absolute-value-function.name: Absolute value function
absolute-value-function.oneLiner: A V-shaped function whose every output is 0 or greater
absolute-value-function.description: The absolute value function y = |x| ignores the sign of the input and keeps only its size. Its graph is a V with its vertex at the origin: it returns x unchanged when x is positive, and with the sign flipped when x is negative.
absolute-value-function.significance: It is the basic tool for expressing situations where only the size matters and the direction does not — distance, error, deviation, and the like.

x.description: The original value, which may be positive, negative, or 0.

|x|.description: The size of x with its sign stripped off. It equals the distance from 0 on the number line.

realWorldExamples: Finding the difference between a below-zero and an above-zero temperature
Measuring how far a value strays from a target (the error)

floor-function.name: Floor function
floor-function.oneLiner: The function that drops everything after the decimal point, rounding down to the nearest integer
floor-function.description: The floor function (a step function) y = floor(x) returns the largest integer no greater than x. Its graph is a staircase, stepping up by one at each integer.
floor-function.significance: It is the mathematical basis for every everyday situation that calls for rounding down — the quotient of a division, banded fares, integer division in computer programming.

x.description: An input value anywhere in the reals.

\\lfloor x \\rfloor.description: The largest integer that is no greater than x. For example floor(3.7) = 3, floor(-1.2) = -2.

realWorldExamples: Working out a banded bus fare (charged in 5km bands)
How many sweets each friend gets when you share them out equally

distance-formula.name: Distance formula
distance-formula.oneLiner: The formula for the straight-line distance between two points on the coordinate plane
distance-formula.description: The distance formula d = sqrt((x2 - x1)² + (y2 - y1)²) works out the straight-line distance between the points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) on the coordinate plane. It is the Pythagorean theorem applied to coordinates.
distance-formula.significance: It is the most basic tool of coordinate geometry and the starting point for many geometric problems, from the side lengths of a figure to the radius of a circle.

d.description: The length of the straight line (segment) joining the two points.

x_1.description: The horizontal position of the first point.

y_1.description: The vertical position of the first point.

x_2.description: The horizontal position of the second point.

y_2.description: The vertical position of the second point.

realWorldExamples: Working out the straight-line distance between two places on a map
Judging the distance between two characters in a game

midpoint-formula.name: Midpoint formula
midpoint-formula.oneLiner: The formula for the point exactly halfway between two points
midpoint-formula.description: The midpoint formula M = ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2) finds the point exactly halfway along the segment joining two points on the coordinate plane. You simply average each coordinate.
midpoint-formula.significance: It is the basic formula for finding the bisection point of a segment, the centre of a figure, a point of symmetry, and it is essential for solving coordinate geometry problems.

M.description: The point exactly halfway between the two points.

x_1.description: The horizontal position of the first point.

y_1.description: The vertical position of the first point.

x_2.description: The horizontal position of the second point.

y_2.description: The vertical position of the second point.

realWorldExamples: Finding a meeting place exactly halfway between two friends' homes
Working out where to put a sign at the centre of a stretch
